preamble: A coda rhotic can assimilate completely to a following bilabial nasal, giving a geminate [mm] (rm > mm). This regressive total assimilation is regular in Middle Indo-Aryan, where Sanskrit karman and dharma became Pali kamma and dhamma, and it recurs in western Cuban Spanish (arma > a[mm]a) and as a one-off in Aleppo Domari. The change is always conditioned by a following m.

examples.note: Middle Indo-Aryan cluster simplification: r assimilates to the following m.
Coda /l/ and /ɾ/ can merge and assimilate to the following consonant, giving geminates; the non-assimilated pronunciation is more common.
Verb borrowed from Kurdish hez kirin 'love'; Herin notes the assimilation of /r/ to /m/ occurred only in that one example.

sources: Herin, B. (2012). The Domari Language of Aleppo (Syria). Linguistic Discovery, 10(2), 1-52. https://doi.org/10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.412
